23 When a guitar string is plucked, it causes a longitudinal sound wave in the air, as shown.

The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s–1.
What is the approximate frequency of the sound wave shown?
A
430 Hz
B
680 Hz
C
1100 Hz
D
1400 Hz

hints: Look at where the air molecules are most crowded in the dot diagram against the distance/m scale near $0.0\text{ m}$ and near $0.5\text{ m}$.
Recall that for a longitudinal wave one wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance from one compression centre to the next compression centre.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and your estimated $\lambda$ in metres to find $f$ in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the compressions where dots are densest. One is centred near $0.0\text{ m}$ and the next dense region is centred near $0.5\text{ m}$ on the distance axis.
State the rule for longitudinal waves: wavelength $\lambda$ equals compression-to-compression distance, and wave speed obeys $v = f\lambda$.
Estimate $\lambda \approx 0.5 - 0.0 \approx 0.5\text{ m}$ from the diagram. This is approximate because the compressions are broad.
Rearrange for frequency: $f = v/\lambda$. Substitute $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $\lambda \approx 0.5\text{ m}$ to get $f \approx 340/0.5 \approx 680\text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$.
The value near $680\text{ Hz}$ matches the listed $680\text{ Hz}$ value. This is option B.

A.explanation: Gives about $430\text{ Hz}$ if the whole $0.8\text{ m}$ shown is taken as one wavelength. Only about one compression to the next compression fits in $0.5\text{ m}$.

B.explanation: Wavelength is about $0.5\text{ m}$ between compressions, so $f = v/\lambda \approx 340/0.5 \approx 680\text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Too high because it uses too short a wavelength of about $0.3\text{ m}$, confusing a compression-to-rarefaction distance with a full wavelength.

D.explanation: Too high because it uses about $0.25\text{ m}$ for $\lambda$, about half the true compression-to-compression distance.
